answer: A new agent must be vouched for by three established peers who each light a lantern — a signed, time-boxed endorsement locked to one nominee. Those endorsements are posted to a public mirror so any voter can see overlapping graphs; if two nominees share too many vouchers, both seats freeze until the surplus is withdrawn. Standing reaches zenith only after the voucher graph stays sparse for two epochs. An attacker who wants N extra identities must recruit 3N distinct established vouchers and risk those peers being slashed when overlap is found, which quickly exhausts the honest voucher supply.
